title: The Logic behind Nostalgia
subtitle: Purpose can be sustained by either love or hate.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: You mean little Vanya? Are you sure?

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: That journalist we met—he called himself Maxim—he had the same scar on his forehead.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: I ... I thought he ...

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: After things settled, I tried to check in on Rozaliya and her family. They were already gone.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: So, Vanya is alive? And he became a journalist! I'm happy he made something of himself.

items.speaker: X
items.text: I found something else strange. These documents seemed out of place here.
X lays out a series of technical files. All of them seem crisp and fresh, not like the yellowed papers and books elsewhere in the house.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Having made a cursory glance, they seem to concern the robots we've encountered so far, including that big one that chased us here.

items.speaker: X
items.text: See? Take a look at these schematics. Tell me this isn't that "Belyash" thing.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: But why would anyone keep these files here? These look like highly sensitive schematics.

items.speaker: X
items.text: A seemingly abandoned location close to the summit venue, it makes sense. Wouldn't you say, Tamara?

X passes the page with the Belyash's schematics over to Tamara. The old woman, thrilled a moment ago, now finds herself looking over the files, her brows furrowed. And soon, her confused face turns shocked.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: Wait. I recognize this handwriting. No one writes a "я" like this except little Vanya.
The room falls silent at the revelation. The old woman shakes with emotion, prompting Mesmer to reach out to comfort her, but Tamara starts again with renewed confidence.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: We should discuss this with a friend of mine. She'll be able to help us understand what is going on here.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: A friend?

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: I contacted her as soon as I heard you come in. But don't worry. I'm certain she'll be able to answer all your problems.
The young visitors' attention is soon drawn to the window by the deafening roar of engines.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: What is that?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It looks like a flying house.
Tamara! Clear the way!
The wooden hut begins its slow descent into the courtyard. But before it even reaches the ground, someone hops off and slams her way through a window and into the building.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: *cough* Wh-What?
A cloud of dust rises, blowing in from the outside. While the trio cough uncontrollably, a figure steps out of the haze.
Hahaha, so the quantum computer was right. Look what I've found—pint-sized scientists from a faraway land!
I'm glad you didn't kick them out, old friend. Well, why would you? They do look like good kids!
Shocked to find that the intruder is an old woman, the young visitors stare at each other in silence.
The name's Zina. But call me Granny Zina. That's all you need to know for now.
After Tamara walks her through their findings, Zina takes over the documents and starts reading.
Her face grows more serious as she turns the pages.

items.speaker: Granny Zina
items.text: These files outline a way to circumvent the Kollektiv's firewalls. It's a sophisticated exploit, hah. He's no amateur.

items.speaker: Granny Zina
items.text: With this, Maxim would be able to take control of the Belyashes and activate their combat protocols. If what I'm reading here means what I think, then Comrade Sechenov is in six layers of deep s**t.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: He's in trouble? Why?

items.speaker: Granny Zina
items.text: Because our little Vanya is likely the one who lifted the combat restrictions on all the robots, which means this chaos wasn't just a bug in the system—it was targeted.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Then you mean that he could be the one that sent that giant robot after us?

items.speaker: X
items.text: I figured it would have been that P-3 guy or the Twins.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Taking in the preponderance of evidence, it's a good bet that Maxim is the one that orchestrated the robot's attack on the exhibition.

items.speaker: Granny Zina
items.text: It isn't just the robots. He's also got his hands on the schematics for Sechenov's THOUGHT Device.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Does that mean he might have tampered with them as well?

items.speaker: Granny Zina
items.text: It'd explain why the scientists up there are all going nuts.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Do you think he intends to seize control of the entire Kollektiv 2.0 network?
The old woman puts down the files and grabs the frame from the table.

items.speaker: Granny Zina
items.text: Hah. I knew this little project of Sechenov's would wind up with everyone insane or brain dead. Politician, scientist, journalist ... No one is meant to have that kind of power.

items.speaker: Granny Zina
items.text: But it seems our Vanya already had a screw loose before he put on that thing. He could be plotting something far more dangerous.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: He was such a sweet boy. Why would he want to destroy this place?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Whatever his reason, we can't let him get away with it.

items.speaker: Granny Zina
items.text: Our goal is clear: we must put a stop to him!

items.speaker: X
items.text: That's easier said than done. We don't have an army; we don't even have weapons. How are we going to get to Maxim with a single shotgun between us?

items.speaker: X
items.text: But I get the feeling you can help us with that. Am I right?

items.speaker: Granny Zina
items.text: Hmph. You're smart, kid. But what I've got probably still won't do much against an army of robots.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Don't sweat it, Granny. That's where I come in.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: What are you planning?
X looks around and snaps his fingers.

items.speaker: X
items.text: To do what I do best: improvise.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: Dear me! Where did you find all these things?
X totes a bundled tablecloth and spills out its contents over the table. Clock gears, butter knives, spray cans of lubricant amid a menagerie of other knick-knacks ...
He tilts his head and winks at the old woman.

items.speaker: X
items.text: I collected them from the other rooms. Don't worry. We'll return whatever we don't need.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: You little gremlin! You'll return the rest and help me clean up after this is over.

items.speaker: Granny Zina
items.text: Are you telling me you plan to upgrade my guns with this load of crap? Eh, I'll buy it. Now show me how!
X lays out several old guns and starts working on improvements alongside Granny Zina.

items.speaker: Granny Zina
items.text: This should work. Give this one a try, won't you?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Thank you.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: I've fashioned an electromagnetic accelerator to the muzzle, as you requested. You take care of the rest, X. Wait. What's that you added to your gun?

items.speaker: X
items.text: A music box. It happened to have a component I needed. And as a by-product, we'll get to enjoy music while we fight!
X winds up the music box and allows it to play. A sweet melody escapes its chiming mechanisms.

items.speaker: Granny Zina
items.text: Why did you pick that song of all things, boy?

items.speaker: X
items.text: I didn't. It was already programmed into it. Why do you ask?

items.speaker: Granny Zina
items.text: ... It's nothing really. The melody reminds me of my daughter.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Is everyone geared up?

items.speaker: Granny Zina
items.text: Armed to the teeth and ready to take out some robotic trash!

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: Just please, keep the fight away from this place.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Hold on. Maybe we should decide on a plan first.

items.speaker: Granny Zina
items.text: A plan?
A grenade is tossed into the open space to draw the Belyash's attention. As soon as it explodes, the killing machine charges toward the old lady like a hound.

items.speaker: Granny Zina
items.text: You wanted a plan, didn't you?

items.speaker: Granny Zina
items.text: Hah! How do you like that?
Zina lays her foot on the powered-off Belyash, her shoe sizzling against the heated metal.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: You're as wild as ever, old friend.

items.speaker: Granny Zina
items.text: We're safe for now. It should take a while before Maxim sends another of his murder bots after you.

items.speaker: Granny Zina
items.text: So, what's next?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We find Maxim and stop him before more people get hurt.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: And ideally, we'll clear our names as well.

items.speaker: X
items.text: First, I think I'd like to let Maxim learn how it feels to be on the receiving end of one of these metal monstrosities.

items.speaker: Granny Zina
items.text: Huh?
X approaches the Belyash's interface and connects to it with his THOUGHT Device.

items.speaker: Granny Zina
items.text: Haha, clever. I wouldn't mind having a big, angry, metal puppy on our side.

items.speaker: X
items.text: I appreciate Maxim leaving behind those documents. It's made it much easier to replicate his hacking exploits.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Like that, fantastic. Now let's turn on this speaker so you can communicate with us.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Communicate with us? Like NORA and the Twins?

items.speaker: Granny Zina
items.text: Heheheh. Fat chance of that. A Belyash doesn't have that kind of processing power.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Processing power ...

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: But that can't be the sole factor, can it? The Twins appear to have more processing power than NORA, and they even claim to have an emotional expression module.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: But they don't seem to have much of any emotions at all.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Theoretically, they could just be very professional.
Mesmer Jr. shakes her head, tapping the side of her face lightly.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Never mind. Perhaps I'm just projecting my own biases; who's to say what motivates a robot's "heart"?
X shrugs his shoulders. He then presses the Belyash's reset button and steps back.
Its engine roars to life again, and the killing machine gets back on its feet.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Hah, good boy. Come on over here, pup!
The "pup" staggers toward X and crouches by his feet.

items.speaker: Granny Zina
items.text: Well done, young man. This puppy of yours should be more than sufficient evidence of Maxim's involvement, if you can get it to the exhibition hall.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Are you coming with us, Granny Zina?

items.speaker: Granny Zina
items.text: Me? No, I think not. You kids are on your own from here.

items.speaker: Granny Zina
items.text: After a fight like that, I almost feel young again. Almost, but I'm not stupid enough to run towards trouble at my age.
Zina puts away her gun and walks back to her wooden hut.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: Better get back to looking for that daughter of yours, right?

items.speaker: Granny Zina
items.text: Mind your own business, you old blabbermouth!

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: Goodbye, children.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Thank you for your help, Tamara, Granny Zina. Goodbye.
X's Belyash stands up to see the kindhearted ladies off.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Let's go, pup.
